overview: Two of the three main components of the cytoskeleton, differing in the protein they're made of and the diameter of the resulting filament.
genZNote: Microtubules: the thick highway pipes. Microfilaments: the thin, flexible support wires.

aspects.label: Protein Subunit
aspects.valueA: Built from tubulin (alpha and beta subunits).

aspects.label: Main Function
aspects.valueA: Forms the spindle fibres, cilia, flagella, and provides tracks for organelle transport.
aspects.valueB: Enables cell shape change, muscle contraction, and cytoplasmic streaming.

aspects.label: Example Structure
aspects.valueB: Actin filaments in a contracting muscle sarcomere.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Microtubules form the spindle apparatus that pulls chromosomes apart during mitosis and meiosis.
overlay.memoryTrick: Micro-TUBE-ules = hollow tubes. Microfilaments = thin threads.
overlay.commonMisconception: Intermediate filaments are a separate, third type of cytoskeletal fibre — don't lump them in with microtubules or microfilaments.
